column4: The national team wins the World Cup. Millions celebrate at the Obelisk and across the country; for a few weeks nobody talks about inflation.
The worst drought in sixty years wipes out the harvest. Billions of dollars in exports are lost.
Extraordinary rains burst rivers and streams. Thousands evacuated and whole neighbourhoods under water.
A grid failure leaves millions without power in the middle of a heatwave. Residents block streets with bonfires.
For the first time since his election, the Argentine Pope tours the country. Huge crowds and a message about poverty no one can ignore.
A newspaper investigation exposes bribes in public works. A driver's notebooks record every bag of cash.
An international miner announces a record investment in a salt flat in the Puna.
With the country cheap in dollars, tourists arrive from all over the world. Bariloche, Iguazú and Buenos Aires are packed.
With prices soaring, crowds loot supermarkets in Greater Buenos Aires, Rosario and Córdoba.
Hundreds of thousands of students, lecturers and families march in defence of public universities. It is one of the largest protests in decades.

column3: An Argentine film wins the Oscar
column4: Argentine cinema wins the award for best international feature once again.
Fire spreads through native forests in the Andes. Firefighters from across the country battle the flames.
The trade surplus breaks records: more dollars come in than in any year in history.
A train with failed brakes crashes into a terminal station. Years of poor maintenance are exposed.
Heads of state from around the world arrive in Buenos Aires for a G20 summit.
